## Reviews
- Code review: traced canonical IDs, projection joins, source modes, retirement, override replay, and navigation end to end. It found stale same-file declaration state, retired-text fallback, an unreplayable split path, and irrelevant call-graph controls; all were fixed and regression-covered. See `.reggie/tasks/code-entity-pages/evidence/reviews.txt`.
- Security review: checked write guards, hostile IDs and paths, source-file boundaries, atomic commit isolation, output escaping, and dependency vulnerabilities. Source reads were tightened to indexed regular files and symlinks were rejected. `npm audit --omit=dev` found zero vulnerabilities.
- Simplification review: confirmed one projection layer, one guarded knowledge transaction, one recursive value renderer, and reuse of the reader/map. No temporary entity compatibility layer or browser parser was introduced.

## Deviations from plan
- The planned file list anticipated changes to `data-concepts.ts` and its tests. The existing builder contract already produced the required stable evidence, so the static/effective concept split was added at the semantic-index boundary instead; this avoided changing the compiler-derived grouping algorithm.
- Ranged source reads were narrowed to tracked first-party JavaScript/TypeScript index files after security review. This is stricter than a generic repository-file reader and matches the program's first-language rollout.

## Discovered issues
- GitHub reported 22 Dependabot alerts on the default branch while this task was pushed. The package-scoped production dependency audit remains clean, and the repository-wide alert triage was captured separately as `github-reports-22-dependabot-vulnerabilities-on` rather than expanded into this task.

## Open risks
- Dynamic dispatch and unresolved callbacks remain explicit findings, so a call page can be incomplete without claiming the missing edge is exact; users see those sites in the unresolved section.
- Unsupported languages still use the existing file-level experience; JavaScript/TypeScript is the only semantic entity implementation in this rollout.
